meta.title: Form Engine
meta.description: A step orchestration engine for multi-step and single-step forms. Owns the flow — you own the fields. Bring any validation library via plugins, or wire in your own form state with FormEngineStep.

blocks.content: Multi-step forms fail in the same way every time. Validation runs too early or too late. Fields from step 1 disappear when the user reaches step 3. The submit handler doesn't know which values belong to which step. The back button wipes state. Zod errors surface on the wrong fields.

The engine solves the orchestration layer. It owns exactly one thing: step flow. Which step is active. Whether navigation is gated by validation. When to call onSubmit. Everything else — field values, error messages, validation logic — lives in your code. Two modes: config-driven (describe fields in a config object and the engine renders them) or headless (put FormEngineStep around your own components and close over your form library's state). Both use the same context and compose with the same plugins.

blocks.title: Plugins compose without interfering
blocks.content: Each plugin's onValidate runs in sequence. If any one returns false or a structured error object, navigation is blocked and errors are set on the form. Multiple plugins can independently gate the same step — the Zod plugin handles schema errors, a server validation plugin checks email uniqueness, an analytics plugin just observes. They don't know about each other.
A three-step account creation form. Steps 1 and 2 have Zod validation — field-level error messages surface automatically. Step 3 is optional and can be skipped.

blocks.label: Interactive demo

blocks.content: The form engine owns exactly one thing: step flow. It tracks which step is active, gates navigation behind validation, and calls your onSubmit when done. Everything else — field values, error messages, validation logic — is yours.

There are two ways to use it. Config-driven: describe your fields in a config object and let the engine render them. Headless: put FormEngineStep around your own components and wire validation yourself. Both modes use the same context and composable pieces.

blocks.title: The engine does not own your form state
blocks.content: react-hook-form runs inside FormEngine and FormEngineRoot by default. In headless mode you bring your own form library — the engine just calls your validate() function before advancing. It doesn't care what's inside it.
Use FormEngine for the batteries-included experience. Describe your steps and fields in a config object — the engine renders progress dots, step title, fields, and navigation buttons automatically.

Use createZodPlugin for per-step Zod validation. Pass a map of step index to schema. Field-level error messages are automatically applied to the form — they appear beneath each field without any extra wiring.

Zod errors are mapped to field keys and set on the form automatically. If a key in your Zod schema matches a field key, its error message surfaces beneath that field. No setError calls, no manual wiring.
Use variant: "custom" to inject any control into the engine. Your render function receives value, onChange, onBlur, error, and disabled — everything you need to wire up any input component.

blocks.title: Error messages surface automatically
blocks.content: If you use createZodPlugin and your schema has a key matching your custom field's key, the error message will appear beneath the field label like any other field. The render function also receives error directly if you want to handle it yourself.
Use FormEngineRoot + FormEngineStep when you want to bring your own form library or render fields yourself. The engine handles step navigation — you handle everything inside the steps.

blocks.title: Works with Formik too
blocks.content: The step's validate function receives no arguments — it closes over your form library's state. For Formik: validate: () => formik.validateForm().then(e => !Object.keys(e).length). For Zustand: validate: () => validateMyStore(). The engine calls it, checks the boolean, and either advances or stays.
Plugins hook into every lifecycle event. Multiple plugins compose cleanly — they run in sequence, and each one can block navigation independently.
Write plugins inline for one-off logic.
Pass mode: "single" to use the engine as a regular form. Progress is hidden and the submit button appears immediately.
Use FormEngineRoot to fully control the layout. Compose progress, step meta, step content, and navigation however you like.
Per-step custom layouts are also available via the layout prop on a step definition. It receives the rendered fields and actions as JSX.

rows.description: All step definitions.
Single hides progress and shows submit immediately.
When react-hook-form validation runs. Only applies in config-driven (field-based) mode — in headless mode, use the step's validate function.
Full-form Zod schema applied on submit. For per-step validation with field-level errors, use createZodPlugin() instead.
Custom react-hook-form resolver. Use this to plug in yup, valibot, or any other resolver.
Unique step identifier. Used by FormEngineStep to match the active step.
Fields for config-driven rendering. Omit when using FormEngineStep with children.
Step-level validation function. Called before plugins. Library-agnostic — close over any form state. Returning false blocks navigation.
Step title shown in FormEngineStepMeta.
Step description shown below the title.
Async guard called after validate() passes. Return false to silently block navigation.
